pr_body:
Fixes #96700 

Replacing the logic that detects mapping-related-subfields (not restricted to multi-field) to determine the right source path for field type lookups.
This logic currently relies on the field full name - it splits at the last `.` character into two parts and if the parent (first part) has a mapping, then the full field name is assumed to be a mapping-related subfield and the parent's source path is used for its type lookup.
The proposed logic relies on mappers instead, thus making it suitable for non-mapping-related cases where both parent and subfield have non-object mappings, which is the use case for which `subobjects` setting was added [in the first place](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/86166).

### Elasticsearch Version

### OS Version

### Problem Description

When setting `subobjects: false`, the `fields` API fails to retrieve subfields.
The `_source` contains the correct subfield value, but the retrieved field gets the parent field's value.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run this test through the yaml test framework:
```yml
  - do:
      indices.create:
        index: test_index
        body:
          mappings:
            subobjects: false

  - do:
      index:
        index: test_index
        refresh: true
        body: >
          {
            "root": "parent",
            "root.subfield": "child"
          }
  - match: {result: "created"}

  - do:
      search:
        index: test_index
        body:
          query:
            term:
              root:
                value: 'parent'
          fields:
            - field: 'root'
            - field: 'root.subfield'
  - match: { hits.hits.0.fields.root.0: 'parent' }
  - match: { hits.hits.0.fields.root\.subfield.0: 'child' }
```

comments: The culprit may be related to a [multi-field handling for source-path resolution during fields values fetch](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/afbf1f5ca182f4fb960efe4826dc633962aaca0b/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/FieldTypeLookup.java#L196-L203)- if the algorithm finds a mapping type for both `parent` and `parent.subfield`, it assumes that this is a result of multi-field mapping, so it returns `parent` as the source path for both. However, when setting `subobjects: false`, it is possible to get `parent` and `parent.subfield` are two real distinct fields, non-related to multi-field mapping, in which case the correct source path for `parent.subfield` is actually `parent.subfield`.

review_comments: Rather than adding an extra map here I think we can extend the use of `fieldToCopiedFields`.  Multifields are essentially a specialised version of copy_to fields after all.
And maybe rename it to something like `sourceLocations` so that it covers both copy_to and multi_field.

@romseygeek I am not sure how nit this would be...
If field `A` is copied to `B`, then we want to be able to tell that `A` is a valid source path for `B`, as well as `B`. If `B` also has a multifield mapping to `B.subfield`, we want to be able to tell that the source paths to `B.subfield` are all `B` source paths. While it's trivial to tell that `B` is a source path for `B.subfield` when going through all mappers, it is not as trivial to tell that `A` is a source path as well. 

To demonstrate, assume that these mappings are iterated in the following order:
1. field `B` mapper is analyzed: 
   - we add a mapping: `B.subfield --> [B]`
2. field `A` mapper is analyzed: 
   - we add a mapping: `B --> [B, A]`
   - we also need to update the former mapping: `B.subfield --> [B, A]`

For every `copy_of`, we would now need to go over all Set values of the new combined map and look for the `copy_of` source field and update the set with the target field if we find such.

While this is definitely doable, it is much less straightforward than the current algorithm, which does't try to maintain copies of same sets for multifields and instead only [resolves this in lookup time](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d36f889003fa39339c9f296117fe5223b4dbe1b8/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/mapper/FieldTypeLookup.java#L200-L205).

Therefore, I still recommend we stick with the additional mapping, but if this doesn't convince you, I will gladly change.

Can we avoid the usage of the variable `fullSubfieldNameToParentPath` entirely? 
My reasoning here is to make usage of the `fullNameToFieldType.keySet()` (`KS` for short) where we should have all the possible parent paths. Therefore a field either has a parent in the `KS` or the path is the field itself.
If that's the case we should be able to find the parentPath by filtering `KS` with just the strings that starts with `field` (parentPath should be a substring of `field`), sorting from longest to shortest to avoid false matching due to ordering (eg. for field `field.subfield` both `field` and `field.subfield` will match and we will always want the longest matching string) and getting the first hit or else `field` itself.
This solution if suitable will also avoid the usage of `FieldMapper#iterator()` that you mentioned above.
To put it in code: 
```
String resolvedField = fullNameToFieldType.keySet()
            .stream()
            .filter(field::startsWith)
            .max(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length))
            .orElse(field);
```

> Can we avoid the usage of the variable fullSubfieldNameToParentPath entirely?

I will look into this, but I think more in the way that @romseygeek [proposed](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97092#discussion_r1254296395)

> Therefore a field either has a parent in the KS or the path is the field itself

If I understand correctly what you mean, this was the problem in the first place- the former lookup assumed that a type mapping to a parent means that the real source path is the parent's path. However, this logic doesn't work with `subobjects: false`, where both `field` and `field.subfield` may have entries in this map and the real source path for `field.subfield` is `field.subfield`, not `field`. 
Sorry if I misunderstood what you meant.

> sorting from longest to shortest to avoid false matching due to ordering

What benefit do we get from replacing a map with O(1) lookup with a computational-heavy operation?

> This solution if suitable will also avoid the usage of `FieldMapper#iterator()` that you mentioned above.

I didn't understand how so, sorry...
I will replace the usage of `FieldMapper#iterator()`, as it seems to be [non-suitable for this purpose](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97092#discussion_r1254447041), but I still need a way to identify mapping-related subfields and relying on prefix is not suitable anymore.

Sorry if I missed what you meant, please try to let me know where I missed.
I'll get back to this next week.
Thanks for the review! 🙏

Thank you for your response and clarification. I understand your concerns about the proposed solution and the performance impact of sorting the keys. At the end I proposed `Stream.max()` instead of sorting that is better but not optimal. 

Considering the limitations you've mentioned, I do agree with you, relying solely on the `fullNameToFieldType.keySet()` it’s not sufficient for correctly identifying real source paths and the use of a prefix-based approach, as you pointed out, may lead to incorrect matches.

After thinking about it some more I do agree with the [solution proposed](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97092#discussion_r1254296395) by @romseygeek. 
I apologise for any confusion caused by my previous suggestion.
I think this can just be `forEach`?

`sourcePathUsedBy()` returns an iterator. 
I could use `fieldMapper.forEach` as it is an `Iterable` before, when I used the default `iterator()`, but I can't anymore

If it has an issue resolving nested fields now, you could add an if condition so that the script either emits `params._source." + name.replace('.', '.?')` or `params._source['" + name + "']`, depending on what's non-null.
I don't think replacing things with `.?` will work here, as internally the values will be a flat map with dots in the keys, not a series of nested maps.
It seems to work well in its current form for both dotted and nested fields, as the test still covers the entire suite and it passes.
It will be so nice to get rid of this, I think it's more or less the last place where we do this annoying dot parsing.
